summary: A village waterfall west of the Girmal country — Dhulda rounds out the Subir belt's falls cluster on the quiet side of the forest roads.
description:
Dhulda hangs off the western side of the Girmal country: a village-land monsoon fall a few kilometres from the U-turn point's river bend, on lanes that see herders more than visitors. It slots into the Subir belt's growing falls circuit — Girmal and the U-turn deck to its east, Karanjwa, Milan, Bhalkhet and Dev Van strung to its south-west — without any of their small fame.

The terms are the belt's usual: short walk in, monsoon-only flow, no facilities, and village directions worth more than any map. Go in the rains or not at all.
highlights: The Girmal country's quiet western fall
Links the U-turn point to the Subir falls cluster

modes.road: Via the Subir–Girmal side roads, west of the Nishana check-post country; ask locally for the Dhulda turn
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Short walk from the village lane; wet-season slick
access.road_condition: Rural tar and dirt; slow in monsoon

visit.notes: Open village land; daylight visits only.

experience.photography_notes: Village fields give the falls a rare open foreground for the belt.

amenities.food: None — Subir or Ahwa have the nearest food

warnings: Wet rock is slick — grip footwear

tips: Fold into the Girmal–U-turn day as the detour nobody else makes
Walk field edges — the approach crosses standing crops in season
